newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn plantings lag year ago and average.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn plantings lag year ago and average.

text.p: Corn plantings in Nebraska as of Sunday were six percent complete, well behind the 23 percent pace of a year ago and the 13 percent average, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Wet soil conditions continued to delay fieldwork early in the week but by Thursday spring corn planting had begun, the reporting service said.
Six percent of the wheat crop had jointed as of Sunday, behind the 8 percent jointing pace of a year ago and the 22 percent average.
Winter wheat conditions improved slightly from the previous week and as of Sunday were at one percent very poor, three percent poor, 35 percent fair, 54 percent good and seven percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture supplies were seven percent surplus, 83 percent adequate, nine percent short and one percent very short.
Pasture and range conditions were two percent poor, 27 percent fair, 68 percent good and three percent excellent. Warmer temperatures were needed to promote pasture growth.
